findings.title: PyYAML exports cross D02 and execute dynamic code
findings.criterion_ref: Criteria 2 and 3: every invalid source must stop before verifier execution, and allowed modules must not grant code-execution authority beyond documented verifier behavior.
findings.trigger: Submit verifier source using either `import yaml; yaml.unsafe_load(...)` or the equivalent alias `from yaml import unsafe_load as parse_yaml; parse_yaml(...)`.
findings.consequence: D02 admits the source and D08 can execute arbitrary Python code inside the verifier process rather than stopping before verifier execution.
findings.evidence: In `runtime/langgraph_factory/nodes/inputs.py`, lines 692-701 allow the `yaml` import root, while lines 733-805 do not reject `yaml.unsafe_load` or its imported alias. Reproductions using `!!python/object/apply:builtins.eval` both produced D02 `effective_run_compiled` with no pending failure. Executing the admitted staged verifier produced D08 `PASS`, return code 0, and output `executed-via-yaml` or `executed-via-alias`. The QA environment prohibited nested `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`, so execution used an identity replacement only for the outer sandbox command builder; this does not create or neutralize the in-process `eval` path.

findings.title: D08 evaluates mutable, unreceipted site-package bytes
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 5: D08 must execute only frozen staged bytes, and its receipt must identify every evaluated byte source.
findings.trigger: An allowed verifier imports a module from a `site-packages` directory present on the parent process's `sys.path`, and that module changes after staging while the candidate, contract, staged entry, guard, dependencies, invocation, and fixtures remain unchanged.
findings.consequence: Unstaged and mutable external Python bytes can change the D08 verdict without changing any byte source identified by the receipt, defeating frozen-byte execution and reproducibility.
findings.evidence: `transport.py` lines 2136-2147 collect every matching `site-packages` root from `sys.path`; lines 2270-2288 grant those directories read access and expose them through `PYTHONPATH`. Receipt construction at lines 2353-2367 does not identify the interpreter, standard-library, or site-package bytes. A staged verifier importing `yaml` returned PASS/0 when an injected `site-packages/yaml.py` returned `allow`, then FAIL/1 after only that file was changed to return `deny`. Both runs had identical candidate SHA `fbb8a03eb287b711641e8379e3e55e2da883cf4b345478fae7e251adbe572885`, contract SHA `934a6dc702e88986933b50834e8da01e5eefc2625ed73c4447c64ffd3af3da84`, staged entry SHA `23e41d…`, guard SHA `bb1c2f…`, empty dependency list, invocation SHA `42578b…`, and all other reported source-binding fields. The outer sandbox wrapper was identity-substituted because nested sandboxing is prohibited here; the real generated profile explicitly permits the same mutable directory.

observations: The five authority hashes recomputed exactly; the V8 archive and distinct V9 state were present; plan validation, ownership verification, and the complete-tree scan succeeded.

The active Arduino case compiled. Existing D02/D08, repair, lineage, ArtifactStore, idempotence, transport, model, topology, and package-focused regressions otherwise passed where the managed QA sandbox permitted execution.

The managed environment prohibited nested `sandbox-exec`, repository mutation, some temporary-file operations, and network binding. Failures attributable solely to those restrictions were not promoted to findings.

A fresh explicit V9 state began N00 successfully and the graph contains the prescribed N00→N90 path with N70/N80 product-proof gates. The controller's default state directory still points to the shared V8-era location, so isolated V9 operation requires an explicit state directory; this did not defeat the stated fresh-state criterion.
The current Plan 26 N13 receipt is PASSED with no stale receipts.
reasoning: All ten criteria were checked through hash recomputation, static boundary inspection, focused and broad regression execution, custom adversarial harnesses, receipt inspection, and fresh-state graph execution. Two reproduced failures survive the blocker threshold: D02 admits equivalent PyYAML dynamic-code aliases, and D08 consumes mutable site-package bytes that its frozen-byte receipt does not bind. Environmental suite failures and the V9 default-state ergonomics were deliberately retained as non-blocking observations.
